title: aidp plan — executable task graph (aidp-plan.v1)
description: The machine-readable plan a `planner` stage writes as `plan.json`. One object per task to realize, each carrying its own self-contained prompt, instructions and write set. `aidp workflow emit` consumes this file to compile the tail of the Workflow: tasks become parallel sub-agent dispatches ordered by `needs`, with extra dependencies inserted automatically wherever two tasks would write the same file. Keep it honest — a task's `files` are the contract that makes parallel execution safe.

schema.description: Contract marker. Optional, but write it — it pins the shape for future revisions.

summary.description: One short paragraph: what this plan achieves overall.

jira_keys.description: The user stories this plan covers.

shared_files.description: Files that several tasks would need to touch (DI registration, module wiring, csproj/serverless entries, .sln). NEVER list these in a task's `files`: no task may edit them. Each task describes the change it needs in `follow_ups`, and the merge sub-agent applies them all once, at the end.

id.description: Short stable identifier, unique in the plan (e.g. T1, T2). Referenced by other tasks' `needs`.

title.description: One line, imperative: what this task delivers.

kind.description: Routes the task to the consuming stage. A pipeline stage may claim a subset via `plan_tasks.kinds`; by default one stage claims them all.

prompt.description: The task's OWN instruction, written for a sub-agent that sees only this text plus the artifact paths of the stage. Self-contained: state the change, the design decisions already made, the patterns/utilities to reuse (with paths), and what NOT to do. Do not write 'as described above' — there is no above.

instructions.description: Ordered concrete steps for this task. One step = one verifiable change.

needs.description: Ids of tasks that MUST finish first (real data/API dependencies only). Do NOT add ordering just to avoid write collisions — declare `files` and aidp serializes those automatically. Every id listed here must exist and the graph must be acyclic.

files.description: The task's WRITE SET: every repo-relative file it will create or modify. This is what makes parallelism safe — two tasks sharing a file are serialized by aidp instead of racing. Never list a `shared_files` entry here. Be exact; a missing path is a lost race.

reads.description: Files the task should read for context (never written).

verification.description: How to check this task alone is correct (command to run, test to add/execute).

acceptance.description: Acceptance criteria this task satisfies, traceable to the US.

jira_keys.description: The US this task contributes to (useful when the run covers several unitary stories).

outputs.description: Artifacts this task writes into the stage directory (optional; the stage's declared outputs stay the merge step's job).
